title: Testing Primes and the Sieve of Eratosthenes
short: n is prime when no prime up to √n divides it; the sieve crosses out multiples to list every prime up to N.
trouble: Students test divisors all the way up to n, or stop before reaching √n. And 1 is not prime.

blocks.html: You met primes in grade 4. Now we need a precise definition and two dependable tools: a test for one number and a way to list all primes up to a bound.

Definitions. An integer $p > 1$ is prime when its only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$. An integer $n > 1$ that is not prime is composite: it can be written $n = ab$ with $1 < a, b < n$. The number $1$ is neither. (Leaving $1$ out is what keeps prime factorizations unique; otherwise $6 = 2 \cdot 3 = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3$.)

You only need to test up to $\sqrt{n}$. Suppose $n = ab$ with $1 < a \le b$. Then $a \cdot a \le a \cdot b = n$, so $a \le \sqrt{n}$. The smallest prime factor of $a$ is at most $a$ and also divides $n$. So a composite $n$ always has a prime factor at most $\sqrt{n}$. Turn that around: if no prime up to $\sqrt{n}$ divides $n$, then $n$ is prime.

blocks.title: A composite in disguise
steps: $221$ is odd, its digit sum is $5$ (not a multiple of 3), and it does not end in $0$ or $5$. $221 = 7 \cdot 31 + 4$ and $221 = 11 \cdot 20 + 1$.

blocks.title: A prime
steps: No prime up to $\sqrt{211}$ divides $211$, so it is prime.

blocks.html: To list every prime up to $N$: write $2, 3, \dots, N$. Circle the smallest number not yet crossed out; it is prime. Cross out its multiples, starting at its square. Repeat. Once the next circled number $p$ has $p^{2} > N$, everything still standing is prime.

blocks.name: nt-sieve

opts.task: Press Next prime until the sieve stops. Why does it stop at 7?

blocks.cap: Crossing out starts at $p^{2}$: a smaller multiple $kp$ with $k < p$ has a prime factor smaller than $p$, so it is already crossed out. After 7, the next prime is 11, and $11^{2} = 121 > 100$.

blocks.title: How far does the sieve go?
blocks.q: To list the primes up to $200$ with the sieve, which primes do you need to sieve with?
steps: So sieve with $2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13$. Every number left after that is prime.

blocks.html: Testing every number up to $n$ (slow, though correct), or stopping too early. Stopping at $11$ for $221$ would call it prime, but $13 \le \sqrt{221}$ still had to be tried. Find the whole-number part of $\sqrt{n}$ first and test every prime up to it. And remember: $1$ is not prime.
A composite $n$ has a prime factor $p \le \sqrt{n}$. So test the primes up to $\sqrt{n}$; to list all primes up to $N$, sieve with the primes up to $\sqrt{N}$.
